packs.name: Frame the problem
packs.tagline: Get the question right before anyone builds a slide.

packs.name: Gather evidence
packs.tagline: Find, test and combine facts you can stand behind.

packs.name: Understand the market
packs.tagline: Size it, segment it, and see who wins and why.

packs.name: Shape the strategy
packs.tagline: Turn analysis into real choices with clear trade-offs.

packs.name: Run the numbers
packs.tagline: Business cases, models and metrics a CFO will trust.

packs.name: Tell the story
packs.tagline: Storylines, slides and memos that get to a decision.

packs.name: Deliver and change
packs.tagline: Plans, roles, risks and the people side of change.

packs.name: Boardroom and governance
packs.tagline: Board papers, oversight questions, risk, ESG and AI governance.

packs.name: AI transformation
packs.tagline: Find, prove and scale AI use cases responsibly.

packs.name: Leader's desk
packs.tagline: Everyday tools for meetings, negotiations and messages.

packs.name: Playbooks
packs.tagline: End-to-end flows that chain several skills together.

skills.title: Problem Statement
skills.summary: Turn a vague ask into one sharp, decision-focused question with scope and success criteria.
skills.tryp: Our CEO says 'we need to fix customer churn'. Help me frame the real problem. We are a B2B SaaS firm, ~2,000 customers, churn went from 8% to 13% in a year.
when: A project or request is starting and the ask is fuzzy ('look into pricing', 'fix churn')
A team keeps debating solutions before agreeing on the problem
You need a one-paragraph brief to align a sponsor before work begins
inputs: The request in the sponsor's own words
Who will make the decision, and by when
What is in and out of scope; known constraints (budget, policy, time)
Any numbers that show the problem today

skills.title: Audience Brief
skills.summary: Profile who you are persuading: what they care about, what they already believe, and what would change their mind.
skills.tryp: I'm presenting a cloud migration proposal to our CFO and the audit committee chair next week. Build an audience brief.
when: Before writing any deck, memo or speech that must persuade
When presenting to a board, investors, a regulator or a new executive
When a past presentation 'landed badly' and you need to know why
inputs: Who the audience is (names, roles, or type)
What you want them to decide or do
What you know about their priorities, history with the topic and style
The format and time you will get

skills.title: Issue Tree
skills.summary: Break a big question into a logical tree of smaller questions you can actually answer.
skills.tryp: Build an issue tree for: why has our hospital's operating margin fallen from 6% to 1% in two years?
when: After the problem statement is agreed and before analysis starts
To split work across a team without overlap
When a discussion goes in circles and needs structure
inputs: The key question (ideally from the Problem Statement skill)
Whether you need a 'why' tree (diagnose a cause) or a 'how' tree (find solutions)

skills.title: Hypothesis Tree
skills.summary: Start from a likely answer, then list exactly what must be true and how you would prove or kill it.
skills.tryp: Hypothesis: we should exit our retail banking business in Country X. Build the hypothesis tree and the tests.
when: You have an informed 'day-one answer' and want to test it fast
Time is short and you cannot analyse everything
You need to show a sponsor what evidence would change the recommendation
inputs: The question and your best current answer
What is known already, and what data is available

skills.title: MECE Check
skills.summary: Audit any list, structure or storyline for overlaps and gaps, then fix it.
skills.tryp: Check this for MECE: our growth levers are 1) new customers 2) digital 3) pricing 4) upselling 5) Asia expansion 6) partnerships.
when: Reviewing a structure, workstream list, agenda or set of options
A slide lists 'key reasons' or 'key drivers' that feel messy
Before you assign work to people (overlap = duplicated effort)
inputs: The list or structure to check
What it is meant to cover (the 'whole')

skills.title: Stakeholder Map
skills.summary: Map who matters, where they stand, and the plan to move each of them.
skills.tryp: Map stakeholders for rolling out a shared-services finance centre across 6 business units. The BU CFOs are sceptical.
when: At project start, or when a decision needs buy-in from many people
When an initiative stalls and you suspect politics
Before a board or SteerCo where someone may block
inputs: The initiative and the decision needed
Names or roles of people involved
What you know of each person's position

skills.title: Engagement Workplan
skills.summary: Turn the issue tree into a week-by-week plan: analyses, owners, data, meetings and deliverables.
skills.tryp: Build a 6-week workplan for a pricing review across 3 product lines, team of 4, SteerCo every 2 weeks.
when: Kicking off a project, study or engagement
Showing a sponsor how the work will reach an answer on time
inputs: Key question and issue tree (or hypotheses)
Fixed dates: SteerCos, board, budget cycle

skills.title: Research Plan
skills.summary: Plan exactly what to find out, from which sources, in what order, before searching anything.
skills.tryp: Plan the research to understand the Indian cold-chain logistics market for a possible investment. I have 2 weeks.
when: Before desk research, due diligence or a briefing
When research tends to sprawl and eat time
To brief an analyst or junior team member
inputs: The question or hypothesis the research serves
Sources you have access to (databases, experts, internal data)

skills.title: Source Validation
skills.summary: Grade every source and claim for reliability so you never put a weak number in front of a board.
skills.tryp: Validate these claims for our deck: 1) the global AI market will be $1.8T by 2030 (from a blog) 2) 70% of transformations fail 3) our churn is 2x industry average.
when: Before key facts go into a recommendation
When a statistic sounds too neat (70% of X fail...)
inputs: Where each came from (links or document names)

skills.title: Research Synthesis
skills.summary: Turn piles of notes, reports and links into a few clear findings with evidence and implications.
skills.tryp: Synthesise these 6 analyst reports and my notes on the EV charging market into key findings for our investment committee.
when: After desk research or document review
When a team has lots of material but no clear message
To brief a busy executive on a complex topic

skills.title: Interview Guide
skills.summary: Write a crisp guide for expert, customer or employee interviews that gets real answers, not opinions.
skills.tryp: Write a 45-minute interview guide for talking to hospital procurement heads about buying AI radiology tools.
when: Expert network calls, customer discovery, employee listening tours
Any interview where you have limited time with a senior person
inputs: Any compliance rules (e.g. no confidential info from experts)

skills.title: Interview Synthesis
skills.summary: Turn many interview notes into patterns, quotes and numbers, with how strongly each is supported.
skills.tryp: Here are notes from 12 customer interviews about our onboarding. Synthesise the findings.
when: After a round of interviews or calls
When you need quotes and patterns for a deck
To compare views across groups (customers vs staff, region A vs B)

skills.title: Survey Design
skills.summary: Design a short, unbiased survey that produces numbers you can actually use.
skills.tryp: Design a 10-minute survey for SME owners in India about willingness to pay for an AI bookkeeping assistant.
when: Customer, employee, pulse or market surveys
When you need numbers from many people, not depth from a few
inputs: Objectives and decisions the survey serves
Target respondents and how you reach them

skills.title: Survey Analysis
skills.summary: Turn survey results into a few significant, decision-relevant insights with honest caveats.
skills.tryp: Here's our employee engagement survey export (CSV, 1,400 responses). What are the real insights?
when: After an employee, customer or market survey
When a team has charts but no clear message
Comparing segments, regions or time periods
inputs: The data (file or table) and the questionnaire

skills.title: Market Sizing
skills.summary: Size a market top-down and bottom-up, reconcile the two, and show every assumption.
skills.tryp: Size the market for AI-powered invoice processing for mid-size companies in India.
when: Checking a market number someone quoted
inputs: The product or service and the geography
Any known data points (prices, customer counts, reports)

skills.title: Customer Segmentation
skills.summary: Group customers by needs and value so you can focus, price and serve them differently.
skills.tryp: Segment our B2B customers (logistics software) — we have revenue, industry, size, products used and support tickets for 800 accounts.
when: Deciding which customers to focus on
Designing offers, pricing tiers or sales coverage
When 'one size fits all' is failing
inputs: Customer data or a description of the customer base

skills.title: Competitor Benchmark
skills.summary: Compare competitors on the factors that matter to customers and economics, and spot where to win.
skills.tryp: Benchmark the top 5 competitors of a mid-size Indian private bank on digital, cost-to-income, CASA ratio and SME lending.
when: Board or investor briefings on competitive position
inputs: Criteria that matter (or let the skill propose them)

skills.title: Five Forces
skills.summary: Judge how attractive an industry is and what drives profits, using the five forces framework with evidence.
skills.tryp: Five forces analysis for the Indian quick-commerce grocery industry.
inputs: Whether you are an incumbent, entrant or investor

skills.title: PESTEL Scan
skills.summary: Scan political, economic, social, technological, environmental and legal shifts, and rank what really matters.
skills.tryp: PESTEL scan for a European pharma company setting up a manufacturing plant in Telangana.
when: Input to scenarios or risk registers

skills.title: Value Chain Analysis
skills.summary: Map where value and cost sit across the chain, and find where to compete, cut or integrate.
skills.tryp: Map the value chain for branded generics pharma in India and show where the profit pools are.
inputs: Cost or margin data if available

skills.title: Jobs To Be Done
skills.summary: Understand the real 'job' customers hire you for, and the outcomes they measure you on.
skills.tryp: What jobs do CFOs hire an FP&A software for? Build a jobs-to-be-done map.

skills.title: Pricing Strategy
skills.summary: Set or reset prices using value, cost and competition, with tiers and a test plan.
skills.tryp: We sell HR software at a flat ₹500/user/month. Help us redesign pricing; margins are falling and big customers get 40% discounts.
when: Launching a product or entering a market
Moving to subscription, usage or tiered models

skills.title: SWOT to TOWS
skills.summary: Do SWOT properly: evidence-based factors, then turn them into concrete strategic moves (TOWS).
skills.tryp: Do a SWOT and TOWS for a regional hospital chain in Tier-2 Indian cities facing entry by national chains.
when: Quick strategic assessment of a business unit
When someone asks for a 'SWOT' and you want it to lead somewhere

skills.title: VRIO Analysis
skills.summary: Test which resources and capabilities give a lasting advantage, and which are just table stakes.
skills.tryp: Run VRIO on our capabilities: proprietary claims data, 1,200 hospital network, in-house underwriting AI, brand in South India.
when: Testing an acquisition or investment thesis
Deciding which capabilities to invest in
inputs: List of resources and capabilities (or let the skill draft one)

skills.title: Growth Options
skills.summary: Lay out all the ways to grow (core, adjacent, new) and size and rank them.
skills.tryp: Lay out growth options for a ₹800 Cr specialty chemicals firm that sells mainly to Indian textile makers.

skills.title: Strategic Options Evaluation
skills.summary: Compare 2-5 real options against agreed criteria, with trade-offs made explicit, and recommend one.
skills.tryp: Evaluate options for our underperforming European subsidiary: fix, merge with UK, sell, or close.
when: Board or ExCo choices between alternatives
When debate is stuck on preferences
Documenting why an option was chosen
inputs: The decision and options (or ask the skill to generate them)

skills.title: Portfolio Matrix
skills.summary: Plot business units or products by attractiveness and strength, and decide invest, hold, fix or exit.
skills.tryp: Here are our 9 product lines with revenue, growth, margin and market share. Build a portfolio matrix and recommend roles.
inputs: List of units/products/projects with data (revenue, growth, margin, share, capital)

skills.title: Scenario Planning
skills.summary: Build 3-4 plausible futures from key uncertainties, and find moves that work across them.
skills.tryp: Build 2030 scenarios for an Indian IT services firm, given uncertainty about GenAI's impact on headcount-based revenue.
inputs: The focal question and time horizon
Key trends and uncertainties (or a PESTEL scan)

skills.title: Build, Buy or Partner
skills.summary: Decide whether to build a capability, acquire it, or partner, with a clear rationale.
skills.tryp: Should we build our own GenAI underwriting assistant, buy a vendor product, or partner with an insurtech?

skills.title: Business Case
skills.summary: Build a decision-ready business case: options, costs, benefits, NPV, risks and the ask.
skills.tryp: Build a business case for automating accounts payable at a 5,000-employee manufacturer: ~180,000 invoices a year, 22 AP staff.
inputs: The proposal and the problem it solves
Cost and benefit estimates you have
Company discount rate (hurdle rate), time horizon

skills.title: Financial Model Spec
skills.summary: Design a clean, auditable financial model: structure, drivers, sheets and checks, ready to build.
skills.tryp: Spec a 5-year financial model for a new D2C skincare brand: revenue by channel, CAC, gross margin, working capital, funding needs.
when: Briefing an analyst to build a model
Fixing an existing model that nobody trusts
inputs: Purpose and decisions the model supports

skills.title: Unit Economics
skills.summary: Work out whether each customer, order or unit makes money, and which levers fix it.
skills.tryp: Our subscription meal kit: ₹2,400 per box, food cost ₹1,150, delivery ₹220, packaging ₹140, discounts avg 12%, CAC ₹1,900, 38% churn per month. Do the unit economics.

skills.title: Sensitivity Analysis
skills.summary: Find which assumptions really move the answer, and what has to be true for the decision to flip.
skills.tryp: Run a sensitivity on this business case: volume 10,000 units, price ₹4,500, unit cost ₹2,900, fixed cost ₹1.2 Cr, capex ₹3 Cr, 5 years, 12% discount rate.
when: To decide which assumptions need more research
inputs: The model or the key formula and base-case inputs
Reasonable ranges for each input (or let the skill propose)

skills.title: Break-even and Payback
skills.summary: Quickly find the break-even volume, payback period and margin of safety for a decision.
skills.tryp: We're opening a new clinic: fit-out ₹1.8 Cr, monthly fixed cost ₹22 lakh, average bill ₹1,400, variable cost 35%. Break-even and payback?
when: Quick screening of an idea or project
New site, product or store decisions
inputs: Fixed costs, variable cost per unit (or %), price per unit

skills.title: KPI Driver Tree
skills.summary: Break a top metric into the drivers people can act on, with owners and targets.
skills.tryp: Build a driver tree for EBITDA margin of a cement plant, down to operational levers.

skills.title: KPI Dashboard
skills.summary: Design a one-page dashboard leaders will actually use: right metrics, targets, layout and alerts.
skills.tryp: Design a monthly executive dashboard for a 300-bed hospital's CEO.
when: Setting up management or board reporting
inputs: Audience and decisions the dashboard supports

skills.title: Cost Take-out
skills.summary: Build a structured cost-reduction plan: baseline, levers, sizing, phasing and risks to service.
skills.tryp: We need to cut ₹40 Cr (8%) from a ₹500 Cr cost base in a retail chain over 18 months without hurting customer experience. Build the plan.
inputs: Cost baseline (by category, function or site)

skills.title: SCQA Storyline
skills.summary: Build the storyline every executive document needs: Situation, Complication, Question, Answer.
skills.tryp: Build an SCQA storyline: we want approval to consolidate 4 regional data centres into one hybrid cloud setup.
when: Starting any deck, memo, board paper or speech
Fixing a draft that is 'all data, no message'

skills.title: Pyramid Structure
skills.summary: Structure any argument top-down: answer first, grouped support, evidence below.
skills.tryp: Restructure this draft email to the CEO into a pyramid: [paste draft].
when: Restructuring a long or rambling draft
inputs: The main message (or let the skill infer it)

skills.title: Executive Summary
skills.summary: Write a one-page executive summary a busy leader can act on in two minutes.
skills.tryp: Write an executive summary of this 30-page vendor assessment for our CIO: [paste or attach].
when: Handing over findings to a busy sponsor
inputs: Audience and the decision they own

skills.title: Insight Synthesis
skills.summary: Turn analysis outputs into true insights: what it means, why it matters, what to do.
skills.tryp: Here are 15 observations from our sales analysis. Turn them into the 4-5 real insights for the leadership team.
when: When a team has findings but no 'so what'
Preparing a board narrative from data

skills.title: Action Titles
skills.summary: Rewrite slide titles so each one states the takeaway, and the titles alone tell the story.
skills.tryp: Rewrite these slide titles as action titles: 1) Revenue overview 2) Customer survey results 3) Cost analysis 4) Next steps.
when: When a deck feels descriptive, not persuasive
Turning an analysis deck into a decision deck
inputs: Current slide titles (and ideally slide content)
The overall message of the deck

skills.title: Ghost Deck
skills.summary: Draft the whole deck as titles and sketched exhibits before doing the analysis, so the work stays focused.
skills.tryp: Build a ghost deck for a board presentation recommending entry into the Middle East market for our edtech company.
when: Early in a project, to focus analysis
Aligning a team on what each person produces

skills.title: Chart Selection
skills.summary: Pick the right chart for the message, and avoid charts that confuse or mislead.
skills.tryp: What's the best chart to show how our cost per claim compares across 12 regions and against the target?
when: Fixing a chart that confuses people
inputs: The message you want to show

skills.title: Exhibit Builder
skills.summary: Design a complete, board-ready exhibit: title, chart, callouts, source, and the code to draw it.
skills.tryp: Build an exhibit from this data showing that 3 product lines generate 80% of our profit: [paste table].
when: Turning data into a slide visual
Making charts consistent across a deck
inputs: Brand colours or template, if any

skills.title: Slide Copy Editor
skills.summary: Tighten slide text: fewer words, clearer claims, consistent style, no jargon.
skills.tryp: Edit this slide text for a board audience: [paste text].
when: Final polish of a deck or one-pager
Making a deck written by many people sound like one voice

skills.title: Deck Quality Check
skills.summary: A senior-partner style review of a deck: storyline, logic, evidence, numbers and visual consistency.
skills.tryp: Do a full quality check on this deck before it goes to the board on Monday: [attach].
when: Last check before a board or client meeting

skills.title: Speaker Notes
skills.summary: Write natural speaker notes and a timing plan, with likely questions and crisp answers.
skills.tryp: Write speaker notes for my 12-slide, 20-minute presentation to the investment committee: [attach deck].
when: When someone else built the deck you must present

skills.title: Decision Memo
skills.summary: Write a crisp memo that frames a decision, the options, the recommendation and what is being asked.
skills.tryp: Write a decision memo for the ExCo: should we move our customer support to a 24x7 model using AI agents plus a smaller human team?
when: Recording why a decision was taken

skills.title: Implementation Roadmap
skills.summary: Turn a recommendation into a phased roadmap with workstreams, milestones, dependencies and quick wins.
skills.tryp: Build an 18-month roadmap to implement a new finance operating model with a shared-services centre in Pune.
when: Board or sponsor asks 'how will this actually happen?'

skills.title: Operating Model Design
skills.summary: Design how the organisation will work: structure, processes, people, technology, governance and locations.
skills.tryp: Design the target operating model for a new AI and data Global Capability Centre serving a US parent.
inputs: Strategy and goals the model must serve

skills.title: RACI Builder
skills.summary: Clarify who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for each activity or decision.
skills.tryp: Build a RACI for our monthly financial close across Group Finance, BU finance, shared services and IT.
when: New programmes, processes or org changes
When decisions stall or get re-opened

skills.title: Change Management Plan
skills.summary: Plan the people side of change: impact by group, messages, training, resistance and adoption measures.
skills.tryp: Build a change plan for rolling out an AI copilot to 3,000 relationship managers in a bank.

skills.title: Risk Assessment
skills.summary: Identify, score and plan responses to the risks of a project, decision or business.
skills.tryp: Do a risk assessment for launching our lending app in Indonesia in 2027.

skills.title: Pre-mortem
skills.summary: Imagine the project has failed, explain why, and fix those causes now.
skills.tryp: Run a pre-mortem: it's December 2027 and our ERP migration has failed badly. Why?
when: Before launching a project or approving an investment
Before a big commitment that is hard to reverse

skills.title: SteerCo Update
skills.summary: Write a crisp steering committee update: status, decisions needed, risks, and next steps.
skills.tryp: Write this month's SteerCo update for our CRM programme from these notes: [paste notes].
when: When status reports are long and say nothing
inputs: Progress notes, milestones, KPIs, risks, issues

skills.title: Benefits Tracker
skills.summary: Make sure promised benefits are defined, owned, measured and actually delivered.
skills.tryp: Build a benefits tracker for our procurement transformation that promised ₹60 Cr savings over 3 years.
inputs: The business case or promised benefits

skills.title: Board Paper
skills.summary: Write a board paper directors can read in 10 minutes: purpose, recommendation, analysis, risks and the resolution.
skills.tryp: Write a board paper seeking approval to acquire a 51% stake in a logistics start-up for ₹120 Cr.
when: Turning a management deck into a board paper
Reviewing a paper before it goes to directors
inputs: Board or committee name and date

skills.title: Board Question Bank
skills.summary: Generate the sharp, fair questions a non-executive director should ask on any paper or topic.
skills.tryp: I'm an independent director. Management is proposing a ₹500 Cr investment in a GenAI platform. What should I ask?
when: Preparing for a board or committee meeting

skills.title: AI Governance Review
skills.summary: Assess how well an organisation governs AI: policy, roles, inventory, risk, controls, and board oversight.
skills.tryp: Review our AI governance. We have 40+ AI use cases, no AI policy, and the data science team approves its own models.
when: Board or audit committee oversight of AI
Preparing for regulation or client due diligence
inputs: Description of current AI use and governance

skills.title: AI Risk Register
skills.summary: Build a risk register for AI use cases: classify, score, control and assign owners.
skills.tryp: Build an AI risk register for these use cases: resume screening, customer chatbot, fraud detection, marketing copy generation, credit limit setting.
inputs: List of AI use cases with a short description

skills.title: Risk Appetite Statement
skills.summary: Draft a board risk appetite statement with qualitative positions and measurable limits.
skills.tryp: Draft a risk appetite statement for a mid-size NBFC with a growing digital lending book.

skills.title: Integrity Check
skills.summary: Screen a plan, proposal or engagement for bribery, money-laundering, tax, health-product, competition and other legal and ethical red lines before it goes out.
skills.tryp: Run an integrity check on this growth plan for a pharma client before it goes to the steering committee. It uses a local facilitator for a hospital tender and a doctors' summit abroad. [paste plan]
when: Growth, sales, pricing, tax or market-entry recommendations
When an agent, intermediary or success fee is involved
inputs: Countries, sector and any government touchpoints

skills.title: ESG Materiality Assessment
skills.summary: Identify and prioritise the sustainability topics that matter most, using double materiality.
skills.tryp: Run a materiality assessment for an Indian auto-components manufacturer exporting to Europe.

skills.title: BRSR Readiness Check
skills.summary: Check readiness for India's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report, including data gaps and assurance.
skills.tryp: Check our BRSR readiness. We're a listed FMCG company; we did BRSR last year but data came from spreadsheets and assurance is coming.
when: Moving to reasonable assurance on BRSR Core
Board or audit committee oversight of ESG disclosures
inputs: Last BRSR (if any) and data sources

skills.title: AI Opportunity Scan
skills.summary: Find where AI can create real value in a function or business, grounded in processes and pain points.
skills.tryp: Scan our finance function (FP&A, AP, AR, close, treasury) for AI opportunities. 120 people, ERP, monthly close takes 9 days.
when: Starting an AI strategy or roadmap
inputs: The business or function, key processes, volumes, systems

skills.title: AI Use-Case Prioritiser
skills.summary: Score and rank AI use cases on value, feasibility and risk, and pick the first wave.
skills.tryp: Prioritise these 15 AI use cases for our insurance company: [paste list].
when: Too many AI pilots and no focus
inputs: The use-case list with short descriptions

skills.title: AI Business Case
skills.summary: Build an honest business case for an AI use case, including model, data, change and run costs.
skills.tryp: Build a business case to scale our GenAI contract-review assistant from 20 legal users to 400 across the group.

skills.title: Data Readiness Check
skills.summary: Check whether the data for an AI or analytics use case is available, good enough, legal to use and accessible.
skills.tryp: Check data readiness for a churn prediction model at a telecom: CRM, billing, network quality and call-centre data.
when: Before an AI or analytics build
When pilots keep stalling on data
inputs: The use case and the decision it supports
Data sources and what you know about them

skills.title: AI Pilot Design
skills.summary: Design an AI pilot that proves value with clear success criteria, guardrails and a scale decision.
skills.tryp: Design a 10-week pilot for an AI assistant that drafts responses to customer complaints at a bank.
when: Before any AI pilot or proof of concept
inputs: The use case and expected value

skills.title: Agentic Workflow Design
skills.summary: Redesign a process for AI agents working with people: steps, tools, handoffs, controls and metrics.
skills.tryp: Design an agentic workflow for intercompany reconciliation across 14 entities in two different ERP systems, month-end close.
when: Moving from RPA to AI agents
Assessing whether a process is ready for agents
inputs: The current process steps, systems, volumes, pain points

skills.title: Responsible AI Review
skills.summary: Review an AI system before launch for fairness, transparency, privacy, safety, security and accountability.
skills.tryp: Do a responsible AI review of our GenAI chatbot that will answer customer questions about insurance policies.
when: Before launching or scaling an AI system
After an AI incident or complaint
inputs: System description: purpose, users, data, model, outputs, decision impact

skills.title: Meeting Brief
skills.summary: A one-page brief before any important meeting: objective, people, positions, your asks and your lines.
skills.tryp: Brief me for a 30-minute meeting with a prospective client's CFO who is evaluating us for a finance transformation.
when: Before client, investor, board or senior internal meetings
When you have 10 minutes to prepare
Briefing a leader who is joining a meeting
inputs: What you know about them and the history
What you want out of it

skills.title: Red-Team Review
skills.summary: Stress-test a plan, argument or document like a tough, fair critic, before your audience does.
skills.tryp: Red-team this strategy: we plan to become the #1 AI consulting partner for mid-market manufacturers in India within 3 years. [paste plan]
when: Before a board, investor or client presentation
When everyone in the room agrees too fast

skills.title: Negotiation Prep
skills.summary: Prepare a negotiation: interests, BATNA, ZOPA, trade-offs, opening position and concession plan.
skills.tryp: Prepare me for negotiating a 3-year renewal with our cloud vendor; they want a 18% increase, our budget allows 5%.
when: Internal negotiations for budget or people
inputs: What is being negotiated and the stakes
What you know about the other side

skills.title: First 90 Days Plan
skills.summary: Plan a new leadership role: diagnose, build relationships, secure early wins, and set direction.
skills.tryp: I'm starting as Head of Data and AI at a mid-size insurer in 3 weeks. Build my 90-day plan.
when: Starting a new role or job
Taking over a team or function
inputs: What you know about the situation

skills.title: Executive Email
skills.summary: Write a short email or message that gets a senior person to read, decide and reply.
skills.tryp: Write an email to our CEO asking her to approve hiring 6 people for the AI programme before the hiring freeze on 1 Dec.
when: Any email to a busy senior person
inputs: What you need and from whom

skills.title: Workshop Design
skills.summary: Design a workshop or offsite that produces decisions, not just discussion.
skills.tryp: Design a one-day leadership offsite to agree our 3-year AI strategy priorities with 14 executives.
inputs: Purpose and the outputs you need

skills.title: Start Here: Toolkit Guide
skills.summary: Not sure which skill to use? Describe your situation and get the right skills in the right order.
skills.tryp: I have a board meeting in 2 weeks to propose a new digital lending business. Which skills should I use and in what order?
when: Unsure which skill fits your task
Wanting a guided sequence for a bigger piece of work
inputs: What you are trying to achieve, for whom, and by when
What you already have (data, drafts, notes)

skills.title: Playbook: Strategy Review
skills.summary: End-to-end strategy review: from the question to a recommended strategy and roadmap, in guided stages.
skills.tryp: Run a strategy review for our ₹1,200 Cr hospital chain: growth has stalled and national chains are entering our cities.
when: New CEO or leader setting direction
inputs: The business and the strategic question
Available data: financials, market, customers, competitors
Timeline and audience for the final output

skills.title: Playbook: Board Pack
skills.summary: Prepare a complete board submission: paper, summary, risks, resolution, and rehearsal of directors' questions.
skills.tryp: Help me prepare the board pack for approval of our ₹300 Cr capex plan for a new plant.
when: First time presenting to a board
inputs: The matter and the decision sought

skills.title: Playbook: Investment Case
skills.summary: From idea to approval-ready investment case: sizing, economics, model, sensitivity, risks and the ask.
skills.tryp: Build the investment case for launching a subscription maintenance service for our industrial pumps installed base.
inputs: Cost, price, volume data or estimates

skills.title: Playbook: AI Roadmap
skills.summary: Build an AI roadmap for a business or function: opportunities, priorities, cases, governance and adoption.
skills.tryp: Build an AI roadmap for the operations function of a mid-size Indian logistics company.

skills.title: Playbook: Market Entry
skills.summary: Decide whether, where and how to enter a new market, from attractiveness to entry mode and launch plan.
skills.tryp: Should our Indian SaaS HR platform enter Saudi Arabia, and if so how?
when: Responding to a partner or acquisition opportunity abroad
